clips.text: Break time! The children queue up to buy snacks at the canteen.
One child rushes in and goes straight to the front.
The others kindly point to the end of the line. So the child waits for a turn too.
Everyone gets a turn. "Thank you!" they say with a smile.
At the warung, Aya sees someone hand back extra change. The seller smiles, relieved.
In the park, a child finds a wallet and gives it back to its owner.
Another child bravely tells the truth about a mistake.
Aya smiles. Honesty can take courage, but it brings a calm heart and people's trust.
On Sunday morning, the neighbours greet each other. Today is the kampung clean-up day.
People bring brooms, hoes and buckets. Everyone joins in, young and old.
The children carry dry leaves together. Heavy loads are lifted in pairs.
When the work is done, someone brings fried bananas and tea for everyone.
The kampung is clean, and neighbours feel closer. That's gotong royong!
After school, a child borrows a storybook from a friend. "I'll bring it back on Monday!" they promise.
On Sunday night, they remember the promise and put the book straight into their bag.
On Monday morning, they set off on time.
The book comes back in good shape. "Thanks for lending it to me!"
The friend smiles. Keeping promises helps people trust us.
That afternoon, a child is sent to buy sugar at the warung. The queue is long.
The busy seller gives back too much change. No one notices.
The child pauses and wonders, "If everyone knew, would I still keep it?"
They hand the money back. The seller says thank you: that money came from a hard day's work.
Since then, the seller always greets them warmly. Honesty builds trust.
The children are building a cardboard tower for a group project.
The tower gets bumped and falls. One child is really angry and wants to shout.
They stop, breathe slowly and count to five.
The friend who bumped it says sorry. "It's okay, let's build it again," comes the reply.
The second tower is even sturdier. Staying calm helps us think clearly.
The class is choosing a place for a field trip. Everyone may suggest one.
Some children talk at once and cut in on a classmate's idea.
One child raises a hand and says politely, "Can we take turns so everyone is heard?"
Now everyone takes turns. The quiet classmate's idea turns out great: the botanical garden!
They decide together. Speaking up politely lets every voice be heard.
In the class group chat, someone posts a classmate's photo with a mean joke.
The classmate in the photo feels embarrassed and sad.
One child pauses before replying. "How would I feel in their place?"
They write, "Let's delete the photo, it's not kind." Then they send their friend a supportive message.
The next day, they play together again. One kind message can change someone's day.
